title: Tech News with G. Dai — Episode 5
intro: Namaste! Welcome to episode five of Tech News with G. Dai. Five stories you need to know today. And the last one is about your phone data!

stories.headline: Google's AI chips now orbit Earth
stories.vo: Wow, AI is now in orbit! Google's first space data center satellite is online, with four T-P-Us on board. Its first job was writing a space poem, and two more satellites launch in twenty twenty-seven.

stories.headline: Linux flaw allows remote root attacks
stories.vo: Server admins, listen up! A new Linux kernel flaw, rated nine point eight out of ten, can give attackers remote root access. Anthropic researchers built a working exploit in about fifty-three minutes. Patches are still rolling out.

stories.headline: Reddit to lock content behind logins
stories.vo: Here's a surprise for Reddit fans! After twenty years of open browsing, Reddit will slowly become a logged-in service. Tests start in coming months outside the U-S, so reading without an account may soon end.

stories.headline: NT fibre plan is hugely popular
stories.vo: Big demand for Nepal Telecom fibre! The thirty M-B-P-S yearly plan costs just rupees four thousand nine hundred ninety-nine, but N-T can connect only about twelve hundred homes a day, so many people are waiting.

stories.headline: NT's NPL pack: 8 GB a day
stories.vo: Cricket fans, this one is for your phone! Nepal Telecom's N-P-L Unlimited Pack gives eight G-B of data every day, plus three hundred thirty-three call minutes, for rupees five ninety-nine. Buy it by Mangsir fifth.

outro: That's your tech brief for today. Which story would you share with a friend? Tell me in the comments, and follow G. Robotics so you never miss tomorrow's brief.
